## Team Skills vs. Market Demand (2024 Postings)

### Market demand from job postings

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

jobs = pd.read_csv("data/jobs.csv", usecols=["SKILLS_NAME", "SOFTWARE_SKILLS_NAME"],
                   low_memory=False)
text = (jobs["SKILLS_NAME"].fillna("") + " " + jobs["SOFTWARE_SKILLS_NAME"].fillna(""))

# display name -> search pattern in the skills text
patterns = {
    "SQL": r"\bSQL\b",
    "Python": r"Python",
    "Tableau": r"Tableau",
    "Power BI": r"Power BI",
    "Excel": r"Microsoft Excel",
    "Data Visualization": r"Data Visualization",
    "Data Analysis": r"Data Analysis",
    "ETL": r"Extract Transform Load|\bETL\b",
    "Statistics": r"Statistics|Statistical Analysis",
    "Machine Learning": r"Machine Learning",
    "Cloud (AWS/Azure)": r"Amazon Web Services|\bAWS\b|Microsoft Azure",
    "Communication": r"Communication",
}

demand = pd.Series({
    name: text.str.contains(pat, case=False, regex=True).mean()
    for name, pat in patterns.items()
}).sort_values(ascending=False)

demand_pct = (demand * 100).round(1)
demand_pct.rename("% of postings listing skill").to_frame()
```

```{python}
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.barplot(x=demand_pct.values, y=demand_pct.index, color="#2C7FB8")
plt.xlabel("% of postings listing the skill")
plt.title("Most In-Demand Skills in Business Intelligence Postings")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Team skill levels

Scale: 1 = Beginner, 2 = Basic, 3 = Intermediate, 4 = Advanced, 5 = Expert.

```{python}
# EDIT: replace names and scores with your real team's
team = {
    "Name": ["Richa", "James", "Ben", "Victoria"],
    "SQL":                [4, 3, 3, 2],
    "Python":             [4, 3, 4, 2],
    "Tableau":            [2, 3, 1, 2],
    "Power BI":           [2, 2, 1, 3],
    "Excel":              [4, 4, 3, 4],
    "Data Visualization": [3, 3, 2, 3],
    "Data Analysis":      [4, 4, 3, 3],
    "ETL":                [2, 1, 1, 2],
    "Statistics":         [3, 3, 4, 2],
    "Machine Learning":   [3, 2, 3, 1],
    "Cloud (AWS/Azure)":  [2, 1, 1, 2],
    "Communication":      [4, 4, 3, 4],
}
df_skills = pd.DataFrame(team).set_index("Name")

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4.5))
sns.heatmap(df_skills, annot=True, cmap="coolwarm", linewidths=0.5, vmin=1, vmax=5)
plt.title("Team Skill Levels Heatmap")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Skill gaps

Required level is scaled from market demand: the most-demanded skill maps to 5, and others scale proportionally. A gap is the required level minus a member's level (0 if they meet it). This is a relative measure, not an absolute standard of expertise.

```{python}
required = (demand / demand.max() * 5)
gap = (required - df_skills[required.index]).clip(lower=0).round(1)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4.5))
sns.heatmap(gap, annot=True, cmap="Reds", linewidths=0.5)
plt.title("Skill Gaps vs. Market Demand (higher = bigger gap)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
summary = pd.DataFrame({
    "Team average": df_skills.mean().round(1),
    "Market-required level": required.round(1),
    "Average gap": gap.mean().round(1),
}).sort_values("Average gap", ascending=False)
summary
```

### Improvement plan

```{python}
top_gaps = gap.apply(
    lambda r: ", ".join(r.sort_values(ascending=False).head(3).index), axis=1
)
top_gaps.rename("Top 3 priority skills").to_frame()
```
